newsitem.title: UK: British Midland owner breaks up group.
newsitem.headline: British Midland owner breaks up group.

text.p: British Midland Airways has been split off from a group of smaller regional carriers to avoid any conflict of interest with arch rival British Airways, it was announced on Monday.

British Midland's owner, Airlines of Britain Holdings Plc (ABH), said that the regional group, which operates BA franchises and comprises Manx Airlines, Loganair, Business Air and British Regional Airlines, has been taken over by ABH's controlling shareholder The BBW Partnership.

"It is a situation that has been looked at for some time to remove any conflicts of interest between the regional operations and that of British Midland and to operate them as two independent operations,' a company official said.
BBW owns 60 percent of ABH and is controlled by ABH chairman Sir Michael Bishop. The other 40 percent of ABH is held by Scandinavian Airline Systems.
The company denied the restructuring had any connection with talks being held between British Midland's owners and German carrier Lufthansa LAIG.F about possible future cooperation.
"Those talks (with Lufthansa)are at far too early a stage to warrant anything like a restructuring of this nature," said a spokesman.
"We have said all along that we are talking to Lufthansa because they approached us and those negotiations are continuing," he said.
He declined to comment on recent industry speculation that Lufthansa wants to take a stake in British Midland.

But Bishop has made no secret of the fact that British Midland has attracted several offers in the recent past because of its coveted position at London Heathrow, where it controls 13 percent of all runway slots, making it the airport's second largest operator after British Airways.
